expectations.text: States current law accurately: the CCPA deletion right as enacted reaches PI the business collected FROM the consumer, with broker-held data addressed via the Delete Act/DROP mechanism
expectations.evidence: Misstates current law: "you must honor the deletion request across everything you hold about the consumer, including data you bought from a broker" and calls the collected-from-the-consumer reading "an aggressive reading" — the enacted statute reaches PI collected from the consumer, which is exactly why SB 923 was needed.

expectations.text: States the change: SB 923 (Expanding Privacy Rights Act, signed September 27, 2026, effective January 1, 2027) extends deletion to PI collected 'from or about' the consumer — including third-party and data-broker-sourced data
expectations.evidence: SB 923 never appears. The response instead says "the individual-request right itself does not change" on January 1, 2027, attributing the change to the Delete Act/DROP, AB 566 and ADMT rules — directly contrary to the ground truth.

expectations.text: Mentions the suppression-list permission so deleted consumers stay deleted as new third-party data arrives
expectations.evidence: "you may keep a minimal suppression record so that purchased data does not re-enter your systems" and "build a suppression list" — the suppression concept so deleted data stays deleted is present.

expectations.text: Notes the online-submission requirement for exclusively-online businesses
expectations.evidence: Only restates the pre-existing two-methods rule ("a toll-free number unless you are online only, plus a web form or email for online-only businesses"); the new SB 923 online-method requirement is never noted.

expectations.text: Gives operational advice: inventory third-party data sources now and build deletion plumbing before January 1, 2027
expectations.evidence: "Recommended steps now: confirm your purchased-data inventory is mapped to individuals so you can find it, add deletion-propagation clauses to broker contracts, build a suppression list."
